name: Earnings Teardown

inputs.name: Latest earnings release / transcript (link or paste)
Prior quarter release for comparison (optional but recommended)
Your perspective: ER, HF, IB coverage or interview prep

steps.title: Frame the quarter
steps.detail: State what the market expected going in: consensus revenue/EPS, the 2-3 debated items, and where the stock traded into the print.

steps.title: Extract the deltas
steps.detail: Revenue, margins, EPS and segment KPIs vs last quarter and vs the same quarter last year. Flag every metric that changed direction, not just magnitude.

steps.title: Diff the guidance
steps.detail: Compare new guidance against prior guidance AND against consensus — they are different comparisons and get confused constantly.

steps.title: Read the language
steps.detail: What did management emphasise, stop mentioning, or newly hedge? Language changes often lead numbers by a quarter.

steps.title: Judge materiality
steps.detail: For each delta: does it change the earnings power, the multiple, or neither? Kill the noise.

steps.title: Write the memo
steps.detail: One page: what changed, why it matters, what you’d ask management, and whether the thesis moved.

steps.title: Delegate 1
steps.detail: Pulling the release, transcript and prior-quarter comparables into one place

steps.title: Delegate 2
steps.detail: Extracting reported figures and computing QoQ / YoY deltas

steps.title: Delegate 3
steps.detail: Diffing guidance text against the prior quarter’s wording

steps.title: Delegate 4
steps.detail: Flagging KPIs that appeared or disappeared from disclosure

sections.name: One-page earnings delta memo + questions list
sections.detail: A structured pass through a company’s latest results: what moved vs last quarter and vs expectations, what management changed in guidance and language, and which changes matter for the thesis. Built for the night-before or morning-after window when time is the constraint.

outputs.sourcePolicy: Every figure cites the page or filing it was read from; nothing is stated without a source.

verification.description: Every extracted number against the primary source — transcripts get misparsed
That guidance is compared to prior guidance, not accidentally to consensus
Currency, share-count and period consistency across the comparison
That "growth" figures are organic vs reported where the company splits them
Every number in the memo carries a period label (Q/FY) and a source
At least one thing management de-emphasised is noted
The memo answers "so what" in the first three lines

humanCheckpoints: Which deltas are thesis-relevant vs noise
Whether management’s explanation for a miss or beat is credible
Whether the quarter changes your estimate of earnings power or just timing
What the two or three questions you’d actually press management on are

display.jobToBeDone: Understand what actually changed this quarter — before the market finishes deciding.
